When we have an inequality involving an exponential function with a positive base, we're allowed to multiply or divide both sides by the exponential function.

Dividing both sides of the given inequality by ${2}^{3x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-25)^{3}\cdot {2}^{3x} & <0 \\ \frac{({x}^{2}-25)^{3}\cdot {2}^{3x}}{{2}^{3x}} & <\frac{0}{{2}^{3x}} \\ ({x}^{2}-25)^{3} & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve the inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{({x}^{2}-25)^{3}} & <\sqrt[3]{0} \\ {x}^{2}-25 & <0 \\ {x}^{2} & <25 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & <\sqrt{25} \\ |x| & <5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $-5<x<5.$
